title: The Empty Witness
premise: Jonah Fairweather, the meticulous archivist of St. Aldhelm's Cathedral, has a private habit of solving the deaths the police file away as accidents — three so far, all quietly, all from paper. When twin letters arrive in his office, one confessing to a fourth death and one promising a fifth, he realizes the writer knows his secret and is playing a game with him as the only audience. The trail leads back thirty years to a fire in the cathedral school and a circle of five friends whose alibis were stitched together by a beloved teacher, Father Ambrose. As the promised fifth death approaches, Jonah discovers the confessor is dying and wants the truth archived before memory fails — but the surviving friends will kill to keep the old lie intact. In the end Jonah must choose between the duty of silence that has protected the cathedral and the love of a woman whose father was the fire's first victim, exposing the truth at the cost of his own sanctuary.
about_author: Wren Iversen is the pen name of a former cathedral tour guide who spent a decade cataloguing parish records and listening to the stories old buildings keep. They write quiet mysteries about people who find truth in paperwork, and live near the sea with an uncooperative cat.

chapters.title: The Fourth Accident
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. In the cathedral crypt office, Jonah catalogs the death of verger Edward Lassiter — a fall on the north stair that doesn't fit the wear on the stone. The beat is quiet unease: the archivist notices what others smooth over.

chapters.title: Twin Envelopes
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Two letters arrive in the same hand: one confessing to Lassiter's murder, one promising that 'the fifth will follow the fourth.' Jonah realizes the writer knows about his three private solutions. Beat: fascination curdling into fear.

chapters.title: What the Police Called Weather
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, with a flashback thread. He revisits his three solved deaths — a drowned organist, a fall from the tower, a 'heart attack' — and lays out the pattern he never reported. Beat: confession of his own complicity in silence.

chapters.title: The Fire of 1994
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Digging into the archive, he finds the school dormitory fire thirty years ago: one boy died, five survived, and Father Ambrose gave every one of them an identical alibi. Beat: the past opening like a door.

chapters.title: Marguerite
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She returns to the city for her father's memorial — the caretaker who died in the 1994 fire, officially blamed on his own negligence. She and Jonah, former sweethearts, meet again in the archive. Beat: old love, old guilt.

chapters.title: Five Names
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. He identifies the surviving circle: now a judge, a developer, a headmistress, a retired policeman, and a monk living in the cathedral cloister. Beat: dread as he realizes the letters are working down a list.

chapters.title: The Judge's Alibi
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. He interviews Judge Halloway, whose thirty-year-old story is word-for-word identical to the others — rehearsed, protected, airtight. The judge warns him off with chilling courtesy. Beat: power as a wall.

chapters.title: Ash in the Margins
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She finds her father's old maintenance logs, missing the week of the fire, and a note in his hand: 'They know I saw.' Beat: grief sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Confessor's Hand
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Handwriting analysis points toward someone inside the church — the ink, the paper, the liturgical calendar used as a code. Beat: the sanctuary itself turning suspect.

chapters.title: Brother Anselm
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. He confronts the monk, the gentlest of the five, who neither confirms nor denies, only says: 'We were children, and Ambrose told us what to say.' Beat: pity entangled with suspicion.

chapters.title: What Ambrose Knew
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Father Ambrose, the teacher who built the alibis, died ten years ago — but Jonah finds his sealed papers in the crypt, donated anonymously. Beat: the archive becoming a battlefield.

chapters.title: The Fifth Name
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Cross-referencing the letters' code, he determines the next victim: the retired policeman, the one who investigated both the fire and Jonah's own three 'accidents.' Beat: racing the calendar.

chapters.title: A Death Interrupted
chapters.summary: Jonah and Marguerite's alternating POV. They reach the policeman's cottage as he's being poisoned; they save him, but he recognizes the killer's silhouette and refuses to speak. Beat: terror and the first real alliance.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The policeman, dying anyway of illness, tells her what the fire covered: the boys started it, and her father saw them and was silenced. Beat: her love for Jonah tested against what the truth will cost.

chapters.title: Sealed Papers
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Ambrose's papers reveal he didn't build the alibis to protect the boys — he built them to protect himself; he was there too, and the fire was his cover for something worse. Beat: the moral ground collapsing.

chapters.title: The Headmistress Confesses
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. One of the five, unable to carry it, admits the letters are hers — she is dying and wanted the truth archived before her memory went, but the others are killing to stop her. Beat: the confessor unmasked, the game inverted.

chapters.title: The Developer's Bargain
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The developer offers Jonah everything — funding, silence about his three unreported solutions, even Marguerite's safety — if the archive stays closed. Beat: temptation, and the choice between duty and love made concrete.

chapters.title: Vespers
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The headmistress is found dead before she can sign her deposition; the letters' promise is fulfilled. Jonah realizes the final target is the archive itself — the papers must burn. Beat: grief and clarity.

chapters.title: The Crypt
chapters.summary: Jonah and Marguerite's alternating POV. The developer comes for the sealed papers; Jonah has already moved them, and the confrontation happens among the tombs, where the first lie was kept. Beat: the climax, truth against survival.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. With the policeman's dying statement and Ambrose's papers, Jonah hands everything to the police — including his own three unreported solutions. Beat: sacrifice of his secret sanctuary.

chapters.title: What the Stone Remembers
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The trials begin; the judge recuses and falls; the monk, finally speaking, testifies. Marguerite buries her father's name in the restored record. Beat: mourning that is also release.

chapters.title: The Empty Witness
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, closing. Reinstated but changed, Jonah reopens the crypt to visitors for the first time in decades. The last letter, posthumous, thanks him for being the one who watched. Beat: quiet peace — memory kept is love kept.
